privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Beyblade X Combo Finder is a free, static website. This page explains what data is processed when you use it, and by whom.
privacy.who.title: Who runs this site
privacy.who.p1: The site is run by a private individual based in Italy as a hobby project. The source code and data are public on GitHub (github.com/albertocabasvidani/beyblade-x-combo-finder); you can contact us by opening an issue there.
privacy.who.p2: The site has no accounts, no forms and no comments: we never ask for your name, email or any other personal information.
privacy.analytics.title: Usage analytics
privacy.analytics.p1: To understand how the search is used (which parts are selected, which filters and periods are chosen, which links are clicked) we use PostHog, hosted in the European Union (eu.i.posthog.com), in cookieless mode: PostHog stores no cookies and nothing in your browser storage, and we never assign you a persistent identifier. Visits cannot be linked across days or devices.
privacy.analytics.p2: Data collected: pages viewed, interactions with the search (parts, filters, period, sort order, combos or blades view, marketplace), clicks on outbound links, anonymised technical data (browser, device type, country derived from the IP address, which is not stored). Session replay may record how the page is used, with typed text masked. Data is kept for one year and used only in aggregate to improve the site.
privacy.ads.title: Advertising
privacy.ads.p1: This site may display advertisements served by Google AdSense. Google and its partners may use cookies or device identifiers to show ads based on your visits to this and other sites, and to measure them. Where required by law (EEA, UK, Switzerland) you are asked for consent through Google's consent message before any personalised ad is shown, and you can change your choice at any time from that message. Your choice is stored by Google in a cookie on this domain (FCCDCF), so you are not asked again at every visit.
privacy.ads.link: How Google uses information from sites that use its services
privacy.affiliate.title: Amazon affiliate links
privacy.affiliate.p1: Some links to parts point to Amazon and carry our Amazon Associates tag. If you follow one, Amazon receives the click and may record it under its own privacy policy; if you buy something we may earn a commission, at no extra cost to you. Affiliate links never influence scores or rankings.
privacy.local.title: Preferences stored in your browser
privacy.local.p1: The site remembers two preferences in your browser's localStorage: the colour theme (light/dark) and the Amazon store you picked. They never leave your device and are not used for tracking. Clearing your browser data removes them.
privacy.local.p2: To send you to the right Amazon store, the site asks cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/trace which country your connection comes from. The answer is a two-letter country code, it is kept only for the current browser session, and no other data is sent. If you pick a store yourself, that choice wins and the country is ignored.
privacy.rights.title: Your rights
privacy.rights.p1: We hold no personal data about you, so there is nothing we could hand over, correct or delete on request. For data processed by Google (advertising) or Amazon (affiliate clicks), please refer to their privacy policies and controls.
privacy.rights.p2: Questions or concerns: open an issue on the GitHub repository linked above.

about.affiliate.text: With "Compare with my parts" on, missing parts get a Buy link to Amazon that carries our affiliate tag: if you buy something we may earn a commission, at no extra cost to you. Affiliate links never influence scores or rankings, which come only from tournament data.
about.title: How Scores Are Calculated
about.intro: Every combo gets a Competitive Authority Score from 0 to 10, built mostly from tournament results: how it places (wins and finals carry more weight), how big the event was, and how widely it shows up across independent events — not just how often it is mentioned.
about.scoring.title: Scoring Method
about.scoring.p1: The score combines three pillars, each weighted by how reliable the source is (tournament databases count far more than opinions):
about.scoring.tournament: Tournament performance: placement-weighted (1st > 2nd > 3rd), scaled by event size and faded over time
about.scoring.expert: Meta presence: usage share and the number of independent events a combo appears in
about.scoring.youtube: Corroboration: how many distinct trusted sources back it, across languages
about.scoring.community: Opinion-only mentions (YouTube, Reddit, theory tier-lists) count, but cannot stand in for tournament proof
about.scoring.p2: Each pillar has diminishing returns, so a combo proven across many events ranks above one that fluked a single small win. The meta shifts fast, so recent results weigh more (75-day half-life).
about.factors.title: What Affects the Score
about.factors.mentions: Placement in tournaments (1st/2nd/3rd) and how often
about.factors.weight: Event size — a major win beats a small local
about.factors.recency: Recency — results fade with a 75-day half-life
about.factors.consensus: Independent events and players running the combo
about.factors.results: Reliability of each source (tournament DB vs opinion)

about.disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
about.disclaimer.text: Scores reflect competitive tournament data and community consensus, not absolute performance. The meta evolves constantly as new parts are released and strategies develop. Use scores as a starting point, and experiment to find what works best for your playstyle.

about.ranking.title: Reading the Ranking
about.ranking.text: The home page ranks combos over the last 30, 90, 180 or 365 days. "Sort by" switches between the score, the number of top cuts (every placement in an event's final standings) and the number of wins. "Show: Blades" adds up all the builds of each blade (for CX combos, the Main Blade) and shows its share of the top cuts; tap a blade to see its builds.
